findings.message: At the end state (t = 1.020408 s, launch speed 5) the ball is back at the launch mark with v = -5 m/s. The arrow runs from y=230 to y=290, which goes below the lane box. The lane box covers y 34 to 266, and the launch line is at y=230. The Motion arrow and the 'a' arrow (to y=278) also go past the lane box. The drawing leaves its own scene, so it shows the ball falling out of the lane.

The Motion arrow scale does not match the gravity arrow scale. For example, v = 5 m/s gives a 60 px arrow, while a = 9.8 m/s^2 gives a 48 px arrow. This is acceptable if the two quantities are meant to be compared only by direction, but the plan does not say so.

At launch speed 8 the ball is at y=60, and its callout is at y=40. This is near the top of the lane at y=34, so the scale is only just big enough. Whether any part is clipped cannot be judged without pixels.
The state word reads 'Apex Reached'. The callout and the readout read 'At the Top'. The wording differs, but this is not misleading.
